preamble: The palatal implosive [ʄ] ends up as the voiced retroflex stop [ɖ]. This is a telescoped outcome in two steps. First, Proto-Eastern Cushitic *ʄ (Ehret's *jʼ) merged with *ɗ throughout Lowland East Cushitic (see ʄ > ɗ). Then Afar and many Somali dialects turned that *ɗ into retroflex ɖ, spelled x in Afar and dh in Somali (see ɗ > ɖ). Ehret (1991) gives Afar x (ɖ) and Somali dh (ɖ) as the regular reflexes of *ʄ, the same as those of *ɗ. Arbore and Oromo stop at ɗ, Yaaku keeps ʄ, and Sidamo has sh [ʃ]. Sasse (1979) does not reconstruct *ʄ, so on his account these Afar and Somali forms continue *ɗ, and the whole correspondence depends on Ehret's reconstruction.
phoneticEffects: Retroflexion, Depalatalization, Loss of Implosion, Merger

examples.to: Afar xabal- [ɖabal-] 'to wave arms and sway in dance', Somali dhabaal-ee [ɖ] 'to incite'
examples.note: Ehret (1991) #150. Sidamo shabbaar- 'to be troubled, agitated'.

examples.from: Proto-Eastern Cushitic *ʄaʕ- 'to descend from a height'
examples.to: Somali dhac [ɖaʕ] 'to fall', Afar xaxxaq 'rock fall, precipice'
examples.note: Ehret (1991) #154. Oromo ɗaw-, ɗaʔ- 'to fall on' keeps ɗ; Sidamo sha'-e 'elevated post'.

examples.note: Ehret (1991) #159. Sidamo shill-i ass- 'to set the teeth on edge'.
